neighbours.label: scale modifiers (' long'-term, short'-range', long'-range') in earth-, climate- and physical-science prose; the same words in business or everyday text stay quiet
fire: Volcanic aerosols can produce long-term cooling of the lower atmosphere.
Satellite records reveal long-term trends in Arctic sea ice extent.
The simulation includes short-range repulsion between neighbouring atoms.
Dust from the Sahara undergoes long-range transport across the Atlantic.
Tree rings preserve long-term variations in summer temperature.
Ocean sediments record long-term changes in the carbon cycle.
The crystal shows short-range order but no periodic lattice.
Forecasters rely on long-range predictions of monsoon rainfall.
quiet: The bank offers long-term loans to first-time buyers.
She signed a long-term lease on the flat above the shop.
The airline bought six short-range jets for its domestic routes.
The striker scored with a long-range shot in the final minute.
They have been in a long-term relationship since college.
The charity needs long-term volunteers for its literacy programme.
The shop sells short-range radios for hikers and campers.
Managers rely on long-range plans for hiring and budgets.

notes: Card: ' long' x6, '-range' x2, plus 'Clim-atic', 'Meteor-ology', GSFC in atmospheric-science passages. Probes: 'long-term shifts in regional rainfall' 0.93, 'short-range interactions between water molecules' 0.58, 'meteorology' 0.39; 'a long walk' 0.03, 'long-term contract' 0.03.
